answer: Anchor each agent identity to a leased coworking desk. The operator checks a government ID in person, hands over a keycard, and logs every entry. After 60 days with check-ins on at least 40 separate days, it signs a tenure certificate the agent posts on chain, and the certificate lapses the day the lease ends. Forging one identity takes $300 a month, a real body walking through the door, and two months of showing up, so 1,000 fakes cost $600,000 and 40,000 trips. It is slow work, like carving a sonnet in marble, and the proof only stands once it reaches its zenith.
